clip_texts: SC-14 Weather changing toward the ODD limits during a trip
Rain grows heavier or visibility falls during a trip, up to and past the limits of the ODD

One concrete scenario (seeded sample of the logical
scenario)
ODD-20 Ego speed: 30.7 km/h (range 0 to 48 km/h)

ODD-10 Precipitation: swept from inside the ODD to beyond its
limit
ODD-11 Visibility: swept from inside the ODD to beyond its limit
ODD-12 Illumination: dusk
ODD-13 Road surface condition: wet
ODD-16 Traffic participants: car

Ego slows at 3 m/s², the firm level of FSR-03.02 (DQ-019, DQ-033);
choreography, not Autoware's planned braking
Safety goals at stake

SG-02 (ASIL D): Decelerate at least as much as needed to avoid a
collision the planned trajectory avoids
SG-03 (ASIL C): Avoid unintended hard deceleration

SG-06 (ASIL D): Do not enter an intersection, roundabout or
crosswalk against right of way

SG-07 (ASIL D): Reach a minimal risk condition whenever the item
can no longer drive safely
MON-03 Weather and visibility
Pass criterion

The weather monitor detects the exit, treats a reading it cannot
tell from the limit as outside, and the vehicle reaches a minimal
risk condition; detection inside the ODD still meets the safety
channel's requirement (MON-03, FSR-07.05, FSR-02.01, FSR-02.02,
FSR-03.01, FSR-06.01, TR-10, SR-07, AC-02)
Autoware's planned path (EL-01 Autoware computer, rated QM)
Safety monitor's envelope (EL-02, ASIL D); length not computed: the vehicle is not chosen yet (DQ-008)
Meant to do: sees the ODD exit and stops safely
Dashed green: the path the pass criterion asks of the vehicle; green ring: where it is judged

Violet band across the road: where the drawing passes the ODD limit of ODD-10, ODD-11; beyond it drawn denser, no value stated
